prompt:
Desktop web application UI comp at 1536 by 1024, not a poster and not a photograph. Product: Infrastructure AI Agent, an operations workspace for multiple bridge inspection runs. Direction: Corridor Command Map, drawing from transport control maps, work-zone boards, route diagrams, and precise engineering interfaces. Restrained palette only: mist gray #E8ECE8 page, near-black green #18231F text, route teal #176B62, work-zone amber #E1B13D, white working surfaces. No gradients, no glass, no decorative imagery, no sample images, no huge headline, no floating card grid.

Composition B: a thin top command bar contains product name, system health, queue count, and a strong New inspection button. Below it, a compact horizontal run strip spans the page like a transit line; six run stops show bridge names and states, with one selected running stop. The main area is a three-column operational layout: left column is a collapsible inspection intake form with asset fields and one media drop zone; middle column is the selected case evidence stream with observation rows and confidence bars; right column is the decision stack with severity, retrieved RAG sources, maintenance plan, and schedule window. A slim workflow route runs vertically between the middle and right columns and indicates current stage. Result section tabs appear above the middle and right content: Observations, RAG, Plan, Schedule, Report, Activity. The report tab has a distinct document icon but is not selected. Use technical route lines, functional amber only for running work, red only for failures, compact sans typography, tabular numbers, square-ish 4-6px corners, and subtle borders. High density, clean alignment, no nested cards.

The first viewport must make multi-run control and one selected inspection understandable immediately. All content should look like an actual operator tool.
